correctness.rationale: The stationary calculation is correct under the stated frozen-basis, constant-gradient assumptions. With the \(45^\circ\)-rotated SPD family, entrywise SOAP normalization gives \(p=(\kappa+1)/(\kappa+1+2\varepsilon)\) and \(r=(\kappa-1)/(\kappa-1+2\varepsilon)\), so the singular values are \(p+r\) and \(p-r\). Direct algebra gives \(\kappa_2=\kappa+(\kappa^2-1)/(2\varepsilon)\) and \(\sigma_{\min}=4\varepsilon/((\kappa+1+2\varepsilon)(\kappa-1+2\varepsilon))\). In the refreshed eigenbasis the update is diagonal and has condition number \(\kappa(1+\varepsilon)/(\kappa+\varepsilon)\). The angular half-saturation law follows directly from the rotated off-diagonal entry. The assigned verifier independently replays these identities over randomized parameters; the proof itself is exact algebra, not numerical evidence.
residual_risks: The mechanism is stationary and two-dimensional; it does not by itself establish training divergence.
The singular perturbation depends on taking the small regularizer limit relative to a nonzero stale-basis off-diagonal.

value.rationale: Basis-refresh frequency is an explicit SOAP design parameter and has current empirical stability relevance. The theorem isolates a sharp spectral failure mode: arbitrarily small fixed basis error can become nearly rank-one when \(\varepsilon\) is smaller than the induced off-diagonal scale, while a refreshed basis remains well conditioned. The closed condition-number and angular boundary-layer formulas provide a natural diagnostic benchmark rather than an arbitrary toy computation.
residual_risks: Practical importance depends on how closely real training intervals approximate the frozen-gradient model.
